newsitem.title: UK: Overseas Shipholding increases ship stakes.
newsitem.headline: Overseas Shipholding increases ship stakes.

text.p: Overseas Shipholding Group Inc has bought the remaining 20 percent stakes in four of its tankers on charter to British Petroleum, the U.S. ship owning group said in its annual report.

"In late 1996 and early 1997, OSG increased its economic stake in four of the U.S. flagged crude carriers on charter to BP by acquiring the remaining 20 percent interest in the vessels from its minority partner, and by acquiring from a financial institution its residual ownership interests in certain of the vessels," the report said.
Overseas Shipholding said the move would enhance returns from the long term charters lifting Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude.
The charters cover the full remaining depreciable lives of the 1970s-built vessels and most of the sixth of its eight U.S. flagged carriers, it added.

Overseas Shipholding earlier said it was, in co-operation with BP, evaluating the design, construction and operational alternatives for replacements to the single-hulled vessels in the ANS trade in line with the requirements of the U.S. Oil Pollution Act of 1990.
Overseas Shipholding also has 10 Aframax vessels operating in a 20 ship pool with Venezuelan state oil group PDV Marina.
The fleet transports increasing crude oil exports from the Latin American producing regions of Venezuela, Mexico and Colombia and the U.S. and Caribbean markets, it said.
